original_question: Problem 7.10 (Á. Pelayo). Can one make progress in counting the number of fixed points by studying the spectrum of the quantisation of µ : M → S 1 ?
target_in_paper: Problem 7.10 (Á. Pelayo) in §7.2, "Inverse problem for quantum integrable systems": "Can one make progress in counting the number of fixed points by studying the spectrum of the quantisation of μ:M→S^1?" The surrounding paragraph makes clear that μ is the circle-valued momentum map attached to a symplectic S^1-action. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct target essentially verbatim: it names Problem 7.10, uses the correct map μ:M→S^1, and asks the exact paper question about counting fixed points via spectral study of its quantisation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))
missing_details: It does not say that μ is not an arbitrary map but the McDuff S^1-valued momentum map associated with a symplectic S^1-action on M. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))

It omits the paper's motivation that this is aimed especially at the non-Hamiltonian setting, where there is no ordinary real-valued momentum map. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))

It does not specify that the fixed points being counted are fixed points of the underlying symplectic S^1-action; the nearby context motivates this by compact manifolds with isolated fixed points and by questions about upper and lower bounds. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))

It omits that the quantisation here is unitary rather than self-adjoint, so the relevant spectral object is the spectrum of a unitary operator quantising μ. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should state at least that one seeks spectral information yielding lower bounds, upper bounds, or exact counts for isolated fixed points when such counting makes sense. This sharpening comes from the immediately preceding sentence about "both upper and lower bounds" and the fact that the paper presents the problem as a fixed-point-counting question for circle actions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))

The nearby sentence about momentum maps M→(S^1)^k×R^n is a harder generalization, not part of the stated problem, so it should remain outside the refined question. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))
refined_question: Let (M,ω) be a compact symplectic manifold equipped with a symplectic S^1-action, motivated in particular by the case in which the fixed points are isolated and the action need not be Hamiltonian. Let μ:M→S^1 denote the associated circle-valued momentum map in the sense of McDuff, and let Q(μ) be a unitary quantisation of μ. Can spectral information about Q(μ) be used to obtain information about the fixed-point set of the S^1-action—at least upper or lower bounds, and ideally the number, of its isolated fixed points? ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))
justification: This is the narrowest paper-faithful reformulation because the draft already matches the official statement almost word for word. The only necessary additions are the hidden assumptions supplied by the surrounding context: μ is the S^1-valued momentum map attached to a symplectic S^1-action; the problem is motivated by the fixed-point-counting problem for compact symplectic circle actions with isolated fixed points; and the quantised operator is unitary. I did not broaden the question to the later sentence about momentum maps M→(S^1)^k×R^n, because the paper explicitly presents that as a more difficult general case beyond this "toy version." ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6158379/))
